design:
Part of the phase 2 dogfooding programme (epic: bn op-igib).

LIGGGHTS/DEM is now on the HTR/pebble-bed critical path, so its public API
needs the same quality bar as the other mature crates — **even though further
physics validation work remains**.

## Current state, measured 2026-09-05

`crates/outram-park-fork-liggghts`:

| property | value |
|---|---|
| version | 0.0.0 |
| `#[test]` markers | 72 |
| **prelude** | **none at all** |
| examples | 2 |
| modules | bonded, boundary, contact, coupling, mesh_wall, particle, rolling, simulation, thermal, thermal_radiation |

**No prelude is the single most predictive defect from phase 1.** Of seven
crates dogfooded, the two worst failures were prelude failures: one imported
*nothing* (empty scope, no error, every later type failing to resolve with a
message pointing at the wrong place), and one exported a `todo!()` that panics.
A crate with no prelude starts from behind both of those.

## Required: an honest maturity declaration

Add to `crates/outram-park-fork-liggghts/CLAUDE.md` a dated entry carrying:

- date declared
- validation / reference basis
- evidence class
- **known limitations**
- **API dogfood status** (a new field; phase 1 declarations did not have one)

**Do not claim broader physical validation than actually exists.** 72 unit
tests is an "unit tests + internal consistency" evidence class, not
cross-code and not experimental. If no DEM reference comparison exists yet
(against LIGGGHTS proper, or a published granular benchmark), the declaration
must say so plainly and name what would close it.

The maturity gate (#58) permits this: it deliberately excludes
published-benchmark agreement as a *precondition*, precisely so that API work
can proceed on crates whose validation is still in progress. What it does not
permit is overstating the evidence.

## Also required

- **A prelude**, covering the whole critical path to running a DEM simulation.
- Both existing examples converted to import from it, as the executable proof
  it suffices.

## Note on scope

Sphere packing does **not** currently live in this crate — see the packing
issue. Whether it should is an architectural question worth deciding
explicitly rather than by default.
title: Declare LIGGGHTS/DEM mature, honestly, and give it a prelude

acceptance_criteria: A committed V&V test + docs entry recording both drivers' k +/- sigma and the sigma-distance for both cases, passing within a stated band on a GPU host and skipping (not failing) when probe() returns None.
description: Tolerance-bounded agreement test: ComputeType::Gpu k_eff vs CpuSingleThread reference on (a) a CSG pincell (via C6) and (b) a packed-sphere delta case (via C7). Documents methodology AND measured results (k +/- sigma both sides, delta-k pcm, sigma-distance) per the V&V doc rule; skips gracefully when no GPU adapter.
title: outram-mc GPU: GPU-vs-CPU parity V&V gate (CSG pincell + packed-sphere delta)

description: Borderline. tampines-steam-tables draws from rust-steam (marciorvneto/rusteam) but is substantially the user's own (uom, IAPWS verification, choked-flow HEM, steam turbine). 'Steam tables' is generic and 'TAMPINES' is the user's own acronym, so it may NOT be an externally-trademarked project name — unlike OpenFOAM/OpenMC/NJOY/DWSIM. User decision needed: rename to outram-park-fork-... or leave as-is (attribute rust-steam in NOTICE/README instead). Do not rename until decided.
title: Decide: does tampines-steam-tables need a fork-prefix rename?

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content: Added LegendMode enum {Off,Compact,Full} (app.rs), default Compact per issue #26. Added PlotLayer.legend_group: &'static str (data.rs) and LayerId::legend_group() (layers.rs) mapping each of the 16 layers to one of 6 buckets, collapsing exactly the families the issue names as its own example ('Isotherms / Quality lines / Saturation dome / Validation points') plus Isobars, Critical & triple point, and Region boundaries for completeness -- the 3 saturation-envelope layers and all 7 reference-data layers each collapse to one bucket since they already share a colour (INK / their own PALETTE entry respectively). Wired into app.rs plot_panel(): Off skips .legend() entirely; Compact renames every series to its legend_group before handing it to Line::new/Points::new so egui_plot's default LegendGrouping::ByName merges same-named entries into one row; Full keeps each layer's own distinct label (unchanged prior behaviour). Sidebar gets a new 'Legend' section with the same selectable_value row pattern as Theme. Added layers::legend_groups_collapse_the_families_issue_26_names test (asserts the saturation/reference collapses + that every built PlotLayer.legend_group matches LayerId::legend_group). Note: the SEPARATE exported-figure legend (figure/layout.rs LegendLayout) is untouched -- it already auto-columns and truncates reasonably and was out of this bead's scope (issue's legend complaints are about the live GUI). Verified: cargo check clean, cargo test --release --example tampines-steam-tables-gui: 27 passed, 0 failed.

title: GUI: legend modes (Off/Compact/Full, default Compact) with grouped auxiliary curves

description:
Closes the gap the compile gate cannot: std::thread::spawn, Instant::now and std::fs all COMPILE for wasm and fail only at run time.

Runner: wasm32-wasip1 under Node's built-in WASI (scripts/wasi-run.mjs, wired as the cargo runner in .cargo/config.toml). Chosen because wasm32-unknown-unknown cannot host a test harness without wasm-bindgen + a browser, while wasip1 shares target_arch="wasm32" so every cfg gate in the workspace applies identically. No extra tooling needed beyond Node.

Caveat recorded in three places: WASI is NOT a browser. It has a clock and a filesystem, so Instant::now and std::fs work there and would not in a browser. What it shares with a browser — and what these tests actually exercise — is the ABSENCE OF THREADS.

Tests added, all passing on BOTH wasm and native (native is the oracle):
  tampines-steam-tables/tests/wasm_smoke.rs   Edwards-O'Brien blowdown physics path, 8 cells / 20 steps
  tampines/tests/wasm_smoke.rs                helium/steam counter-flow steam generator (3-crate composition)
  boon-lay/tests/wasm_fallback.rs             rayon ensemble -> serial shim, bitwise reproducibility
  njoy-outram-park-fork/tests/wasm_fallback.rs BROADR Doppler broadening -> serial shim, order preserved

FINDING — dev-dependencies are invisible to the --lib compile gate. Every one of these tests initially failed to BUILD, not to run, because eframe pulls wgpu and wgpu-hal is not Sync on wasm. Dev-deps apply to tests as well as examples, so a crate can pass check-wasm.sh and still be untestable on wasm. Fixed by extending the existing cfg(not(target_os="android")) dev-dependency gates to also exclude wasm in tampines-steam-tables, tampines, boon-lay, outram-mc-libs, tuas_boussinesq_solver, teh-o-prke and outram-park-fork-cfmesh.

FINDING — cargo builds every bin when running any test in a package. njoy's njoy-tui binary uses ratatui/crossterm, which has no wasm backend, so it blocked the njoy test. Fixed with the Android-stub-main shape CLAUDE.md already prescribes, applied per item plus a wasm stub main. Deliberately NOT gated off Android — a TUI is Android-in-scope and is the whole point of that binary.

FINDING — outram-park-mpi's datatype layer runs on wasm but the threads-as-ranks runtime TRAPS (wasm 'unreachable') at the first multi-rank collective. That is correct and expected: the crate implements MPI ranks as OS threads and there is no single-threaded fallback to degrade to. No test was added asserting a trap; see the separate note in the epic.

description: Low-priority follow-ups from the 2026-08-07 bookkeeping pass. (1) The crate now has TWO unit-annotation styles: code-span backtick [m] (152 sites converted) and escaped \[K\] (used consistently in fv_options/ and interface/, renders fine, left alone to avoid churning accurate docs) -- normalise fv_options/ and interface/ to the code-span form in a dedicated sweep. (2) docs/porting-roadmap.md now explicitly marks these as NOT verified: ODE order/stiffness tests, flux->reconstruct roundtrip, discrete divergence theorem, MAX_ITER exhaustion path, scaled-pivoting path, mixture-blending invariants (no mixture module found -- possibly misfiled; check before implementing). Verify or prune each. (3) Rustdoc finding worth preserving: relative intra-doc paths in module //! docs do not resolve in this crate; use crate::-qualified paths (all 2026-08-07 fixes do).
title: basic-lib: doc/test hygiene follow-ups (unit-annotation style, unverified roadmap items)
